We have guidance: steps forward: 1) carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse order: Starting from target, we need to break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and amine? Actually reverse of sulfonamide formation: target contains sulfonamide linking an aniline (the first phenyl with methyl) to sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So retrosynthesis: disconnect S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline. But we can propose sulfonyl chloride precursor: p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) with sulfonyl attached to that phenyl. The sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl (tolyl). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl? Wait structure: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) and the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl (aryl sulfonyl). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) where Ar is the second phenyl with the unsaturated amide side chain. So step 1 retrosynthesis: break S-N bond to give aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (toluidine). The aniline is p-methyl aniline (p-toluidine). So we can propose that.

Step 2 retrosynthesis: The unsaturated amide side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . This is an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to second phenyl. The forward step is amide formation from carboxylic acid and amine. So reverse: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline attached to phenyl). The amide is between carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amine is an aniline (aniline). So we get α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to second phenyl (aryl-CH=CH-COOH). That's product of Doebner modification from aldehyde and malonic acid. So step 2: break amide to give α,β-unsaturated acid and aniline.

Step 3 retrosynthesis: The α,β-unsaturated acid derived from Doebner: we need to get aromatic aldehyde (the second phenyl with aldehyde) and malonic acid. So reverse Doebner: break C=C double bond and carboxylate to give aldehyde and malonic acid. The product is the aldehyde attached to phenyl (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) with the same substitution pattern (the aldehyde at para position relative to sulfonyl? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached at para to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The double bond is attached to phenyl at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES shows c2ccc( /C=C/ C(=O)N... ) cc2. So the aldehyde precursor would be c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (para-aldehyde). So we can propose that.

Thus final route: target -> (1) sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine; (2) α,β-unsaturated acid + aniline; (3) aldehyde + malonic acid.
